name: mcpfold SEO iterative loop
description: One SEO element improved per iteration. Items too large for a single iteration are recorded here with enough detail to be picked up cold on the next iteration. Update `status` and `iteration` as items land.

items.title: Per-URL sitemap lastmod from content, not the build clock
items.problem: Every URL in every child sitemap carried the same BUILD_DATE. Google discards lastmod entirely when a site stamps all URLs identically on each deploy, so the crawl-scheduling signal was worthless across ~hundreds of pSEO pages.
items.solution: scripts/lastmod.mjs maps each route to the source file(s) that produce it and dates it from the last commit touching them (git log -1 --format=%cs), cached per file, falling back to the build date when git is unavailable. Child sitemaps now carry the newest lastmod they contain.
items.verify: node scripts/lastmod.mjs --self-test; e2e 'sitemap lastmod is per-URL content dating'

items.title: Rasterize per-page OG cards to PNG
items.problem: gen-og.mjs emits dist/og/<route>.svg and gen-seo.mjs wires it into og:image and twitter:image for every route. Facebook, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Slack and Discord all REJECT image/svg+xml for og:image, so every page except the home fallback (/og.png) currently renders a blank social card. The code comment in gen-og.mjs already flags this as a deferred follow-up.
items.solution: Add @resvg/resvg-js (or sharp) as an apps/site devDependency; rasterize renderOgSvg() output to 1200x630 PNG in the gen-seo route loop, write dist/og/<route>.png, and point og:image/twitter:image at the PNG. Keep the SVG alongside for debugging. Embed the Inter font bytes or fall back to a system sans that resvg can resolve inside CI containers (resvg does not inherit browser font fallback). Add og:image:width/height/alt per route, and an e2e assertion that og:image ends in .png and returns content-type image/png.
risks: resvg native binary must resolve on the Cloudflare Pages / CI build image
font availability in the build container

items.title: RSS feed is invalid and undiscoverable
items.problem: feed.xml emits <pubDate>2026-01-05</pubDate> — RSS 2.0 requires RFC-822 dates, so readers and Google's blog discovery reject or mis-sort the items. The channel also lacks <language>, <lastBuildDate>, <atom:link rel="self">, and nothing in <head> advertises the feed (no <link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml">), so it is effectively unlinked.
items.solution: New scripts/feed.mjs (pure, self-tested) renders the feed: rfc822() converts frontmatter dates to GMT RFC-822 without day-shifting date-only values, an unparseable date drops the pubDate rather than emitting garbage, and the channel now carries atom:link rel=self, language, lastBuildDate (newest post, not the build clock) and guid isPermaLink. index.html adds <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml> so the feed is discoverable from every prerendered page, not just /blog.
items.verify: node scripts/feed.mjs --self-test; e2e 'feed.xml is valid RSS with RFC-822 dates'

items.title: JSON-LD points at /docs, which is not a route
items.problem: softwareApplication() in src/seo/jsonld.ts sets softwareHelp to `${SITE_URL}/docs`. There is no /docs route in App.tsx and it is not in allRoutes(), so the structured data advertises a 404 on every page that emits the SoftwareApplication node.
items.solution: Added validateJsonLdUrls + internalUrlsIn to scripts/seo-audit.mjs: walks every JSON-LD node a route emits, collects internal absolute URLs (normalizing trailing slash, query and hash, ignoring @context and external sameAs/license links), and fails the build on any that is not in allRoutes(). entry-server.tsx now returns jsonLdNodes alongside the serialized tags so the audit reads structure rather than re-parsing HTML. softwareHelp fixed to /guides.

items.title: No Organization/WebSite node with sameAs + SearchAction
items.problem: Entity consolidation for a brand query ('mcpfold') depends on a site-wide Organization node with sameAs links (GitHub, npm, X) and a WebSite node carrying @id, publisher, and inLanguage. Verify what jsonld.ts already emits site-wide and fill the gaps.
items.solution: Emit a single Organization + WebSite pair on every route with stable @id URIs, and cross-reference them from the page-type nodes via isPartOf/publisher so the graph is connected rather than a bag of disjoint nodes.

items.title: Title/description length guards in the build audit
items.problem: auditMeta checked presence and uniqueness but not length. Measured against the real data: comparison intros ran to 591 chars, feature taglines to 298, use-case taglines to 213, glossary definitions to 195 — all used verbatim as <meta name=description> against a ~155-char SERP budget. Comparison titles hit 71 chars once the ' · mcpfold' suffix was appended to an already-61-char metaTitle.
items.solution: clampDescription() in meta.ts trims to the last whole sentence that fits 155 chars, falling back to a word-boundary cut with an ellipsis when the opening sentence overruns or is too short to fill the snippet (MIN_USEFUL=100). Applied inside meta() so no new page type can skip it; full prose still renders in the page body and JSON-LD. withBrand() appends the brand suffix only when it fits within 60 chars and the title does not already say mcpfold. auditMetaLength() enforces both at build time with a warn tier (>60 title, >155 description) and a fail tier (>70/>180/<50). Verified: every description now lands in 104-154 chars.

items.title: Internal linking: no programmatic related-pages mesh
items.problem: Directory entries, guides, glossary terms, comparisons, features and use-cases are separate silos. Deep pSEO pages get little internal PageRank and no topical cross-linking, which is the single biggest lever on a large generated site.
items.solution: Build a related-links resolver (category siblings, glossary terms mentioned on a page, the guide for a client referenced by a directory entry, the feature a use-case leans on) rendered as a 'Related' block on every deep page. Add a build guard for orphan routes: every route in allRoutes() must be reachable by at least one in-body internal link from another prerendered page.

items.title: Orphan-page + internal-link-graph build guard
items.problem: Nothing verifies that prerendered routes are actually linked from the site. A route can be in the sitemap and reachable only by direct URL.
items.solution: Parse the prerendered dist/**/index.html for internal <a href> targets, build the link graph, and fail the build on orphans, on links to non-existent routes, and on any page with zero outbound internal links. Depends on SEO-7 landing first so the guard passes.

items.title: Breadcrumb JSON-LD coverage across every deep page type
items.problem: BreadcrumbList is mentioned in the jsonld.ts header comment; confirm it is emitted for every deep route (directory entry, category, guide, glossary term, comparison, feature, use-case, blog post) and that positions/URLs are correct. Breadcrumbs drive the SERP path display for deep pSEO URLs.
items.solution: Derive breadcrumbs from the route segments via one shared function and assert coverage in the build audit: every route with 2+ segments must emit a BreadcrumbList whose last item URL equals its canonical.

items.title: Canonical/trailing-slash and host normalization at the edge
items.problem: The prerender writes /x/index.html, so both /x and /x/ serve 200 with the same canonical. Duplicate URLs still burn crawl budget even when the canonical is right. www vs apex and http vs https need a single 301 target too.
items.solution: Add Cloudflare Pages _redirects (or a Worker) normalizing trailing slashes, www→apex, http→https with 301s, and an e2e that asserts the redirect chain is at most one hop.

items.title: Heading hierarchy audit on prerendered HTML
items.problem: No guard that each prerendered page has exactly one <h1>, that it is non-empty, that it contains the page's focus keyword, and that heading levels do not skip.
items.solution: Extend the build audit to parse dist HTML for the heading outline and fail on violations.

items.title: Image SEO: alt text, dimensions, lazy loading, modern formats
items.problem: No audit of in the prerendered output for missing alt, missing width/height (CLS), missing loading="lazy" below the fold, or legacy formats.
items.solution: Add an image audit to the build guard and fix offenders; ship AVIF/WebP with fallbacks where the asset pipeline allows.

items.title: Core Web Vitals budget enforced in CI
items.problem: Rankings are gated on field CWV; there is currently no LCP/CLS/INP budget in CI and no render-blocking-resource check on the prerendered pages.
items.solution: Add Lighthouse CI (or a Playwright + web-vitals harness) against `vite preview` of dist/ with per-route budgets, run on PRs, failing on regression. Preload the LCP image/font, inline critical CSS, and defer GSAP where it is not above the fold.

items.title: GEO: llms.txt completeness and per-page AI answerability
items.problem: scripts/gen-llms.mjs exists but its coverage against allRoutes() is unverified, and answer engines favour pages that state a direct answer in the first 200 words with a scannable definition block. FAQ coverage (src/seo/faq.ts) is partial.
items.solution: Audit llms.txt for full route coverage in the build, extend FAQ coverage to every deep page type with real questions from the keyword map, and add a lead-answer paragraph pattern to the page templates.

items.title: Keyword map → page coverage gaps and cannibalization
items.problem: validateKeywordPages only proves each mapped page exists. It does not prove the reverse — that every meaningful keyword cluster in src/seo/keyword-map.ts has a page — nor does it detect two pages targeting the same primary keyword (cannibalization).
items.solution: Invert the check: report clusters with no page, and fail on two routes sharing a primary keyword. Produce a build-time coverage report to drive the next content batch.
